title: Sajid Nadiadwala to Make Big-Budget Lalit Modi Biopic; Ranveer Singh Eyed for Lead
excerpt: Pinkvilla reports Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment is developing the IPL founder's life story with Sneha Rajani scripting — and Modi himself says Ranveer Singh visited him in London to discuss the role.
body:
• Producer Sajid Nadiadwala is developing a big-budget feature film on the life of IPL founder Lalit Modi under the Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment banner.
  • Writer-producer Sneha Rajani, formerly of Sony, is leading the scripting process; the project is still in development with the makers insisting on "getting the story right" first.
  • Lalit Modi himself confirmed to ANI that a biopic is underway and revealed Ranveer Singh travelled to London to discuss playing him: "Ranveer wants to play me."
  • The film would trace Modi's arc from IPL architect to one of Indian cricket's most controversial exiles — a story that has defeated at least two earlier biopic attempts.

From IPL commissioner to biopic subject

Producer Sajid Nadiadwala is developing a feature film based on the life of Lalit Modi, the Indian Premier League founder whose rise and fall remains one of the most dramatic sagas in Indian sport and business, Pinkvilla reported in an exclusive. The project, being developed under the Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment banner, will trace Modi's journey from architect of the IPL to a central figure in one of the most debated chapters of Indian cricket administration.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=OCRL72Zwpvs

Writer and producer Sneha Rajani — who formerly ran Sony Pictures Networks' film business — is attached to the biopic. A source told Pinkvilla: "Lalit Modi's life has so many different chapters that there is a lot to explore… idea is to tell the story on big screen while also getting into the man behind the headlines. Writing and development are currently being worked on, and the makers want to get the story right before taking it forward."

Modi's own confirmation — and the Ranveer Singh twist

The Pinkvilla exclusive corroborates what Modi himself has said. Speaking to ANI earlier this year, Modi confirmed that work on the biopic was underway and described an extensive research and scripting process: "There is (a biopic in works). It's all being scripted right now. I've already sat through hundreds of interviews... I have a whole team under Sneha Rajani, who used to run Sony... But they're just scripting the story now."

"Ranveer wants to play me. He came and saw me. He said in his life, if there was one role he wanted to play, it would be Lalit Modi as commissioner."

— Lalit Modi

Asked who he would like to see play him, Modi revealed that Ranveer Singh had personally reached out — and travelled to London, where Modi has lived in exile since 2010, to discuss the role. "One day, I get a call saying Ranveer wants to see me. And he comes to London to see me a few years ago, two years ago," Modi recalled, adding that he found Singh "amazing" and praising his recent work.

A story that has resisted filming

A Modi biopic has been announced before and never materialised. In 2009, Percept Picture Company announced "The Commissioner," a fictionalised take on his life, with Shridhar Raghavan scripting — it never went to the floor. Producer Vishnu Vardhan Induri, of '83 fame, later announced plans to adapt Boria Majumdar's "Maverick Commissioner" into a feature film. And speculation continues around whether Arjun Rampal's upcoming Hansal Mehta OTT series "Billionaire" draws on Modi's life, though the makers have stayed silent.

The material is undeniably rich: Modi built the IPL into a multi-billion-dollar global spectacle, was suspended by the BCCI in 2010 amid financial irregularity allegations, and has lived in London ever since, an outsized presence on social media who has never returned to face Indian authorities. It is the rare story with sport, boardroom intrigue, exile and a protagonist still active in public life — precisely the kind of content cinema Nadiadwala has balanced lately, from Housefull 5 and the multi-ending experiment to Bawaal, Chandu Champion, Super 30 and Chhichhore.

What to watch

Everything hinges on the script — and on casting. Ranveer Singh's reported interest gives the project star momentum, but no deal has been announced, and the makers have made clear they will not rush development. For the diaspora, the IPL's creation story is also the story of how Indian cricket became the world's richest sporting league — a biopic that gets it right will matter well beyond the box office.
